notes.title: Free Ride mode coming to Mafia: The Old Country as a free update
notes.content:
[p]As our first order of business, we'd like to thank you, our passionate and fiercely loyal community, for making the launch of [i]Mafia: The Old Country [/i]a success. We're truly humbled by all the support and dedication that defines the [i]Mafia [/i]fandom; you are the reason we get to craft these gritty crime dramas, and we're eternally grateful.[/p][p][/p][p]Now that the game is finally in your hands, we're excited to confirm that [b]Free Ride mode will be coming to [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] via a free update for all players in the coming months[/b], which will add new activities and gameplay content. We'll have more details to share at a later date.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157904/caa2f997ab76684ed238c3b8d9684c453b6f5146.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]In the meantime, even after you've experienced Enzo's descent into the criminal underworld of 1900s Sicily, there's already plenty of reason to revisit the the Valle Dorata, whether it's to hunt down hidden collectibles in Explore mode or replay the story with the full Sicilian voiceover. Whichever you do, you'll still have every outfit, collectible, car, Charm, and other unlock earned during your first playthrough.[/p][p]
Since launch, [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] has garnered more than 3 million hours of viewership on Twitch, and players have quickly amassed some dizzying statistics:[/p][list][*][p]600 million shots fired[/p][/*][*][p]185 million enemies dispatched [/p][/*][*][p]17 million bandages used[/p][/*][*][p]10 billion Dinari “earned”[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]For those of you who have yet to uncover the origins of organized crime, [i]Mafia: The Old Country [/i]is available now. Also be sure to check out our list of [u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1941540/view/523098989784990067"]Quick Tips[/url][/u] for how to survive and prove your worth to the Torrisi family.[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1941540/Mafia_The_Old_Country/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Recreating 1900s Sicily in Mafia: The Old Country
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=amarmiKaV2w;full][/previewyoutube]

Throughout the entire [i]Mafia[/i] series, the settings have always been just as important as the protagonists, with Lost Heaven, Empire Bay, and New Bordeaux being as central to the series' identity as Tommy, Vito, and Lincoln. [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i]'s striking new backdrop of early 1900s Sicily is no exception, with its distinct topography providing a whole new experience compared to the dense American metropolises players have visited in past [i]Mafia[/i] games. The rough-hewn beauty of Sicily's rugged countryside is a stark contrast to the grimy urban alleyways that [i]Mafia[/i] fans are familiar with—but the treachery, violence, and complex history of this gangland run just as deep.


[h1]Going Back to Where it All Began[/h1]
As the home of this story and its new antihero, Enzo Favara, the rarely seen Sicilian setting provides a breathtaking new perspective on the series' recurring themes, as well as the origins of the Mafia itself. "The most important thing for us was to make sure [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] was an extension of the games we've made so far," says Game Director Alex Cox, who points out that the franchise has already been to Sicily in [i]Mafia II[/i]. While revisiting the previous titles during the development of 2020's [i]Mafia: Definitive Edition[/i] and [i]Mafia: Trilogy[/i], the team was fully immersed in what makes the classic [i]Mafia[/i] formula great, priming them to translate those same creative pillars into a bold new location.

"Putting our story in rural Sicily, where the Mafia began, necessitated changes in how we approach aspects of the game," Cox continues. "It informed its look and feel, vehicles, weapons, the story itself and its locations. We had to begin by asking, 'Where and how did these criminal traditions begin, and in the context of designing an interactive crime drama, what makes Sicily special?'"

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45157904/7f41adb993537f66d554a9e25efc67c0e62fdcf3.jpg[/img]
[h1]Bringing History to Life[/h1]
As with every [i]Mafia[/i] title, authenticity is a critical component of realizing this believable setting, and the Hangar 13 developers went all-out when it came to real-world research. In addition to digging up rare photos and written accounts from the period, and consuming every popular book or film portraying the Sicilian Mafia, a group of team members and photographers traveled to Sicily to gather the rest of their copious reference material.

Partnering with Italian development studio Stormind Games, they were led on a thorough tour through every type of rural and urban locale depicted in [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i]. The images and audio captured were so richly detailed that some of the areas you'll explore in-game feel like they could've been pulled from the real world. "A lot of the Sicilian countryside still looks today like it did back then, so it's easy for us to get great visual references," says Associate Design Director Zammit.


By exploring the environments that make up the actual Sicilian landscape, the team saw for themselves that it's far from uniform. Their in-person and at-home research helped them identify and recreate these diverse, overlapping settings, which include lush countryside and coastal terrain, ancient ruins, and exquisitely detailed villas. "It was important for us to break down what exists in real life and approach each area individually," says Executive Producer Devin Hitch. "Once we started to blend those together, you could seamlessly move through all of these areas in one vast-yet-varied map." The rare blend of rugged nature and relatively modern architecture is true to the era, and a prime example of what makes [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i]'s turn-of-the-century mob story stand out.


[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45157904/6b554906a251fd993af8301db37038b53077b092.jpg[/img]
[h1]Authenticity Informs Everything[/h1]
"There were times on the trip where you would turn a corner and step into the period of our game," says Art Director Steve Noake. "Almost every detail was exactly as you would expect to see it, especially in the rural locations—but also in the little towns and cities we visited." In those urban spaces, the team says they found nearly the full range of architectural details we see in-game, as well as local experts with intimate knowledge of the region's time-honored craftsmanship.


"We went to a small machine shop where this older gentleman and his son make traditional Sicilian knives," Noake says. "Every region has a slightly different approach to knife-making, so you can almost place each blade in the same way you could geographically place a bottle of wine." Though the delicate art of knife-making has deep roots in Sicilian tradition, today, only a handful of people still craft these weapons for collectors around the world.


[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45157904/0179d1ad9db6271120ed0e08991831c8973ff707.jpg[/img]
The painstaking accuracy of this research informs every aspect of [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i], particularly the new gameplay and storytelling possibilities it affords. On a foundational level, properly realizing 1900s Sicily provides essential context for the game's narrative, character motivations, and the Mafia's seldom explored early days. Beyond that, staying true to history helped guide other creative decisions throughout development, like the focus on knife combat and turn-of-the-century travel methods, that cement the game's identity as something distinct from what you've experienced before.

"There aren't many games where you see horses riding alongside cars on the road," says Zammit. "One thing that makes [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] different is its depiction of this historical junction point where agricultural and urbanized life come together." While past [i]Mafia[/i] titles let you move through relatively small rural areas, putting the countryside at the core of this experience is another way this game recontextualizes familiar elements to make them feel new. Whether it's the refreshed environments, more dynamic traversal options, Enzo's period-accurate arsenal, or just the way characters speak and move, Hangar 13's holistic approach to realizing Sicily makes it far more than just a gorgeous backdrop.

It won't be much longer until you can explore this setting yourself when [b][i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] launches August 8, 2025.[/b] It's available for pre-order and pre-purchase now, and be sure to keep an eye out for future Dev Diary articles diving deeper into the making of this unique Sicilian crime drama.

notes.title: Mafia: The Old Country is available for pre-purchase, launching August 8!
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UOIg2lFVsJE

[i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] is now available for pre-purchase on Steam. The game will offer two editions, [i]Standard Edition[/i] and [i]Deluxe Edition[/i], both of which release on August 8, 2025.

We're also excited to reveal that [i]Standard Edition[/i] and [i]Deluxe Edition[/i] will be priced at $49.99 and $59.99 respectively.* [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] is a compelling story that doesn't require a massive time commitment, and we believe these prices reflect the value of this highly-polished linear narrative experience.

Uncover the origins of organized crime in this gritty mob story set in the brutal underworld of 1900s Sicily. Fight to survive as Enzo Favara and prove your worth to the Cosa Nostra in this immersive third-person action-adventure set during a dangerous, unforgiving era.

Enzo will do anything for a better life. After a brutal childhood of forced labor, he's ready to risk everything to become a man of honor in the Torrisi crime family.

His oath to the Cosa Nostra, with all the power, temptation, and hardship it entails, is a burning reminder of this simple truth:

[b]Family Takes Sacrifice.[/b]

This thrilling narrative is brought to life by stunning visuals, cinematic storytelling, and the authentic realism that the critically acclaimed [i]Mafia[/i] series is known for. Enzo's story unfolds in a time when skill with a stiletto blade was a deadly asset, a [i]lupara[/i] sawed-off shotgun was a go-to firearm, murderous vendettas raged for decades, and mafiosi patrolled their protection rackets on foot, horseback, or behind the wheel of turn-of-the-century motorcars.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45157904/7efb125b6ee696625f3f107f7fa36b0c31542893.png[/img]

[h1]Pre-Purchase Bonus**[/h1]

Pre-purchase [i]Mafia: The Old Country Standard[/i] or [i]Deluxe Edition[/i] to receive The Soldato Pack, featuring weapon and character cosmetics, along with a helpful Charm that Enzo can equip for a passive in-game effect.**
[h2]The Soldato Pack contains:[/h2]
[list]
[*] "Soldato" Outfit
[*] "Scannaturi Speciale" Knife
[*] "Tesoro" Horse and Accessories
[*] "Lupara" Charm
[/list]
[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45157904/00595ccbd7ca859ffa448cd730d1da86e2c2ab25.png[/img]

[h1]Deluxe Edition[/h1]

[i]Mafia: The Old Country Deluxe Edition[/i] lets you descend into Sicily's criminal underworld in true Cosa Nostra style with a variety of bonus items for your collection.

[h2][i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] Deluxe Edition includes:[/h2]
[list]
[*][h3] Full base game[/h3]
[*] [h3]Padrino Pack***[/h3]
[list]
[*] "Lupara Speciale" Shotgun
[*] "Vendetti Speciale" Pistol
[*] "Immortale" Charm
[*] "Padrino" Outfit
[*] "Stiletto Speciale" Knife
[*] "Eckhart Speciale" Limousine
[*] "Cosimo" Horse and Accessories
[/list]
[*] [h3]Gatto Nero Pack***[/h3]
[list]
[*] "Bodeo Nero" Pistol
[*] "Velocità" Charm
[*] "Gatto Nero" Outfit
[*] "Carozella Nero" Race Car
[/list]
[*] [h3]Bonus Materials***[/h3]
[list]
[*] Digital Artbook
[*] Original Score
[/list]
[/list]
In addition to the full base game, purchasing [i]Mafia: The Old Country Deluxe Edition[/i] also grants you the Padrino Pack and the Gatto Nero Pack, plus digital Bonus Materials.***

The Padrino Pack lets you outfit Enzo with an ornate arsenal and accoutrements befitting a godfather with the special weapons, cosmetic items, and Charm that provides a passive in-game effect. The Gatto Nero Pack also lets you outfit Enzo like a member of an exclusive club with a special weapon, cosmetic items, and a Charm that provides a passive in-game effect. 

Additionally, the [i]Deluxe Edition[/i]'s included Bonus Materials, available in-game at launch, let you listen to the sweeping original score of [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] with the official soundtrack, and browse a digital artbook full of gorgeous concept art with behind-the-scenes insights from the developers. The original score for [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] was composed by BT, aka Brian Transeau, and was performed by the Czech National Symphony Orchestra. It also includes a number of traditional Sicilian folk songs, arranged by Peter McConnell and performed by a selection of Sicilian and American musicians.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45157904/c0b75f7366595e269c4c53c9b4aaa95749c8203d.png[/img]

[h1]2K Account rewards[/h1]

To expand your in-game collection even more, [url=https://mafia.2k.com/2k-account-rewards/]signing up for a free 2K Account[/url] earns you the "Garzia Tumulto" Race Car in-game reward, and playing past [i]Mafia[/i] titles while logged into a 2K Account will unlock additional rewards, as detailed in this [url=https://mafia.2k.com/the-old-country/news/mafia-franchise-loyalty-rewards/]Mafia Franchise Rewards[/url] article. Along with these items, signing up for a 2K Account also lets you sign up for newsletters, unlocking the "Lupara Tradituri" Shotgun and ensuring that you stay informed of all the latest [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] reveals.**** 

Also be sure to check out our [url=https://mafia.2k.com/the-old-country/faq/]updated FAQs page[/url], which addresses all of our most commonly asked questions about [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i].

And if you couldn't make it to our PAX East Developer Panel, catch up on everything you missed in our official recap [url=https://mafia.2k.com/the-old-country/news/pax-panel-family-takes-sacrifice/]here[/url]. Hosted by Kinda Funny's Greg Miller, longtime [i]Mafia[/i] developers from Hangar 13 gave an in-depth look back at the history of the franchise, as well as glimpses at how they brought 1900s Sicily to life in [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i].

notes.title: The Team Behind Mafia: The Old Country Heads to PAX East!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157904/965ba7cd91fcd67ca265daf13929d3432aceeaf9.png[/img]
Mafia fans understand the seriousness of breaking Omertá, so don't miss this chance to learn more about [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] at [b]PAX East[/b]!

On [b]May 8[/b] at [i]7pm BST[/i] and [i]2pm ET[/i], watch as Hangar 13 developers debut a new Gameplay Trailer and offer a rare behind-the-scenes look into this storied franchise, live from their panel discussion via the [url=https://www.twitch.tv/pax]PAX East Main Stream[/url] and the [url=https://www.youtube.com/@mafiagame]Mafia YouTube[/url] channel. We’ll also be sharing a dedicated Steam post where you can watch our [b]PAX East[/b] broadcast, streaming live right here on Steam! That post will be made at a later time.

We'll be hosting a special developer panel featuring the talented team of Hangar 13. Whether you're joining us live in Boston or tuning in from the comfort of your own home, you won't want to miss this!
[h1][b]MEET THE DEVS[/b][/h1]
Meet the team who will be attending [b]PAX East[/b]!
[list]
[*] [b]Studio President[/b], Nick Baynes
[*] [b]Game Director[/b], Alex Cox
[*] [b]Cinematics Director[/b], Tomas Hrebicek
[/list]
During the panel, we'll be revealing brand new details about [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i] and giving you an exclusive behind-the-scenes look at the development process, officially ending Omertá.

[h1][b]Q&A: SUBMIT YOUR QUESTIONS![/b][/h1]
Not only are we discussing and showcasing new developments within [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i], we would also like to open the floor to the community to ask us any burning questions you may have! Please use the Steam comments down below to leave your questions and the development team may answer them live at [b]PAX East[/b]!

[h1][b]RULES OF THE Q&A[/b][/h1]
[list]
[*] Please keep your questions relevant to the Mafia franchise or [i]Mafia: The Old Country[/i].
[*] You may ask multiple questions, but please don’t spam comments, please!
[/list]

In-person attendees might also expect a little reward for their show of loyalty, and for those who can't make it to Boston, be sure to check our social channels for additional news coming out of the convention.

We'll see you there, Mafiosos!
